newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 6.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The government has decided that the trial of the persons responsible for the killing of independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and other national leaders in 1975 would be held in civil court.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has refuted allegations against her Awami League government of curtailing facilities for the armed forces.

At least 15 million people in the country's northern and southern parts are at risk of arsenic contamination, said Health Minister Salahuddin Yusuf. He said government had so far identified at least 680 people affected by arsenic poisoining.
A World Bank team has made a survey on developing cooperation among Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan and parts of India in the sectors of trade, transport, energy and water resources.
A court on Tuesday acquitted former President Hussain Muhammad Ershad of a charge of corruption in the purchase of dredgers for Chittagong Port in 1982.

Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Tuesday announced a set of fresh measures, including reduction of the day-to-day price movement limit of traded stocks to five percent from existing 10 percent, to cool down the overheated market.
Asian Development Bank has approved $196.3 million in soft loan for Bangladesh for construction of approach roads in the Jamanu Multipurpose Bridge Project.
